collection.description: Just for a moment. The elders say a carver's hands sometimes know things the carver doesn't.

ask.text:
(carver) has been carving masks out of driftwood all season, and lately (carver.he/she) has started saying that the masks are telling (carver.him/her) who they're for. Today (carver.he/she) comes to find (subject) with a new one, painted in red and white. "This one's yours," (carver) says. "It told me. Put it on. Just for a moment."
The elders say a carver's hands sometimes know things the carver doesn't. The mask's face looks a little like (subject), and a little like someone else entirely.
Should (subject) put it on, or politely hand it back?

c1o1.text: When the mask comes off, everyone gasps. (subject)'s face has changed. It's still (subject), still the same eyes and the same smile, but the shape of it is different: like the mask, or like a cousin of (subject)'s that nobody has ever met. (carver) nods, satisfied. "Told you," (carver.he/she) says. "It was yours."

c1o2.text: The mask comes off, and (subject) looks exactly as before. But on the back of the mask, scratched in the wood where nobody saw it before, is a name, and (subject) can't stop saying it. "Obi," says (subject), if (subject.he/she) is a man; "Itchi," if a woman. "That's me, isn't it?" Within a week, everyone is calling (subject.him/her) by it, and (subject.he/she) answers to nothing else.

c1.text: (subject) ties the mask on. It's warm inside, warmer than wood should be, and it smells of salt and smoke. (subject.He/She) counts to three and takes it off...

c2o1.text: In the morning, (carver) comes out of (carver.his/her) hut with a new face: (carver.he/she) put the mask on (carver.himself/herself) in the night, just to see. "It must have been for me after all," (carver.he/she) says, a little sheepishly. Nobody can quite get used to it. (carver) loves it.

c2o2.text: (carver) leaves the mask on the beach, facing the sea, and goes back to carving bowls. In the morning the mask is gone. A few days later a fisher says (subject.he/she) saw something red and white bobbing out by the reef, facing the island, but nobody goes to look.

c2.text: "It's beautiful," says (subject), "but I like my own face." (carver) looks hurt, and then thoughtful, and takes the mask away. That night (subject.he/she) can't stop looking at it...
